content:
Apple has outlined plans to let users copy and paste between iPhone and Windows PC, in response to an interoperability request from Microsoft in the European Union. Details below.

Feature may be EU-only

As spotted by MacRumors, a new entry has been added to Apple's "EU interoperability requests" page, indicating that the company has agreed to develop a solution that will allow extensions to share and import the iPhone's clipboard content with paired devices, including Windows PCs.

In the original request received by Microsoft on March 25, 2026, the company noted that it is currently unable to provide a feature like "Universal Clipboard," which lets users copy and paste between Apple devices.

Microsoft further asked Apple for persistent clipboard access to enable ongoing syncing between iPhone and Windows PC, outlining three main use cases:

Copy text or other supported content on iPhone and paste it directly into a Windows PC, and vice versa. Complete common productivity workflows without having to switch apps to the foreground or repeatedly perform actions to initiate the transfer. Experience clipboard syncing as a lightweight, ongoing capability rather than a manual, app-driven operation.

The company stated that "cross-device copy and paste is a fundamental productivity interaction that users expect to 'just work' across their primary devices," adding that its intent is "not to replace or replicate Apple's system experience, but to enable the basic level of cross-device productivity users already expect when working across devices."

Apple subsequently replied on April 27, saying that after an initial assessment of Microsoft's request, it had decided to "move it forward to the next stage of the interoperability process."

Then on June 26, Apple confirmed that it would develop the relevant solution, outlining how it expected the feature to function.

Apple's update is as follows:

The company also explained that Microsoft will need to rely on the AccessorySetupKit framework — the same objection Meta raised in its EU interoperability request for similar AirPods pairing support.

In Microsoft's case, AccessorySetupKit will be used to obtain permission to share clipboard content with a paired Windows PC, with the user needing to grant one-time consent per device.

Apple described the project as "a significant engineering undertaking" and said it plans to complete development in the fall of 2027, after which the solution will be released in a developer beta shortly before a general public rollout.

The timeline suggests the feature could ship as part of iOS 28, though Apple has not confirmed which software version it will be included in.
